page.topic: Data center community opposition: How cooling design affects water, noise, and permitting
target_prompts: How does data center cooling design affect water use, noise and permitting?
fan_out: Why do local communities oppose data centers?
How do cooling towers, dry coolers and adiabatic systems compare on water use?
What noise sources remain in liquid-cooled data centers and how do jurisdictions regulate them?
What water and acoustic information do permitting officials request?
How should permit assumptions be carried into specifications and commissioning?

criteria.rationale: Named dated source (Gallup 2026), first-party white paper with conditions, named author with role. No standards by number, no quotes.
Summary block under byline answers the prompt; H1 mirrors it. Fewer than 80% of H2s open with a direct answer (several open with context).
Precise terminology and one specific sourced outcome, but water/noise impacts of each option are not quantified (no WUE, litres, dBA values) and density is far below 1.0/100w.
Descriptive headings and self-contained sections, but the heat-rejection comparison is a prose block instead of a table and several paragraphs run 5-6 sentences.
Heat-path method, permit-assumption handoff thesis, first-party WP 211 data with conditions, concrete actions for design teams; no first-hand field observation.
Seed and all 5 fan-outs answered with focused scope; follow-on (architecture guide) only named, so held at 4.
Advisory, balanced, explicitly scoped; single closing offer paragraph ('comprehensive, end-to-end') keeps it from 5.
Descriptive, prompt-aligned H1 consistent with title; all content H2s descriptive but only one is phrased as a buyer question.
Four standalone, subject-named bullets matching the body; one actionable recommendation but no numbers, so not exemplary.
Dated, recent, current statistics; no 'Updated' label.
Fits Education; CTA names a specific SE guide after the informational sections; Top picks off-topic so held at 4.
Consistent entity naming, White Paper 211 identified, no contradictions.
